style: Use a top-down dark medieval fantasy roguelike style. Use strict pixel art with a transparent background. Do not feather edges, blur edges or anti-alias. Keep every frame consistent in design, scale, palette, equipment and lighting. Leave clear transparent space between sprites. Do not add labels, borders, grid lines, scenery, cast shadows or detached decorative effects.
reference: Use the uploaded base image as the exact character-design reference.

templates.base: Please create a single full-body 32x32-ready sprite for {{name}}, a {{subject}} in a top-down roguelike. Description: {{description}} The sprite should face south/down and have a clear readable silhouette. {{style}}
templates.large: Please create one larger full-body examine-screen image of {{name}}, a {{subject}}. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} Preserve the same proportions, colours, clothing, equipment and personality, but add readable detail suitable for an examine screen. Keep the whole figure visible. {{style}}
templates.walk: Please give me a 16-sprite spritesheet for this {{name}} {{subject}}. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} I need a 4-frame animation for walking north, east, west and south in a top-down roguelike. Arrange the sprites as four rows of four, read left to right: north on row one, east on row two, west on row three and south on row four. Make the footsteps and body movement clearly animate while preserving the exact same design in all 16 sprites. {{style}}
templates.melee: Please give me a 16-sprite spritesheet for this {{name}} {{subject}} performing a melee attack. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} I need a 4-frame attack animation facing north, east, west and south. Arrange the sprites as four rows of four, read left to right: north on row one, east on row two, west on row three and south on row four. Show anticipation, the attack swing or strike, impact follow-through and recovery. Keep the weapon and character consistent in every frame. {{style}}
templates.cast: Please give me a 16-sprite spritesheet for this {{name}} player character casting a spell. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} I need a 4-frame casting animation facing north, east, west and south. Arrange the sprites as four rows of four, read left to right: north on row one, east on row two, west on row three and south on row four. Show a readable wind-up, magical action and recovery, but keep magical effects attached closely enough that each complete frame remains one separable sprite. {{style}}
templates.mine: Please give me a 16-sprite spritesheet for this {{name}} player character mining with a pickaxe. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} I need a 4-frame mining animation facing north, east, west and south. Arrange the sprites as four rows of four, read left to right: north on row one, east on row two, west on row three and south on row four. Show the pickaxe being raised, swung into the target and recovered. Keep the pickaxe and character consistent. {{style}}
templates.shoot: Please give me a 16-sprite spritesheet for this {{name}} player character shooting a bow or crossbow. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} I need a 4-frame shooting animation facing north, east, west and south. Arrange the sprites as four rows of four, read left to right: north on row one, east on row two, west on row three and south on row four. Show aim, release and recovery. Do not draw detached flying projectiles; the game handles those separately. {{style}}
templates.rest: Please give me an 8-sprite rest spritesheet for this {{name}} player character. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} The first four frames should show the character settling down from standing into a resting position. The final four frames should form a seamless repeating idle activity, such as reading a book, tending equipment or quietly resting. {{style}}
templates.death: Please give me an 8-sprite death-animation spritesheet for this {{name}} {{subject}}. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} Start alive and standing, then show a clear progressive collapse, ending completely still on the floor. Keep the final pose readable from the top-down game view. Do not add gore, debris or scenery. {{style}}
templates.deathfire: Please give me an 8-sprite death-by-fire animation spritesheet for this {{name}} {{subject}}. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} Start alive and standing, then show the character catching fire and progressively collapsing, ending completely still and visibly burned. Keep flames close to the body so each frame remains a single separable sprite. {{style}}
templates.wake: Please give me an 8-sprite waking animation spritesheet for this {{name}} creature. Description: {{description}} {{reference}} Begin with the creature squatting, curled up or resting, then show it progressively standing and becoming alert. End in the same upright south-facing stance as the base sprite. {{style}}
